# Projection CLI experience commands

## Overview
How the Projection CLI treats Project evidence, executable MathDocs, Skill Proposals, projections, installation, and work-item completion. Structural commands are deterministic, offline, and stdlib-only; `check-math` executes trusted Project Python and therefore requires the Project derivation environment.

## Principles
- Projected references are package-consistent: a link whose target is not in the same package (drafts, other-audience notes) is demoted to bold plain text; `generate` warns on stderr naming each demoted link. Code fences, external URLs, and non-Markdown targets are untouched.
- Notes may declare `evidence: [paths]` (Project-root-relative). `validate` fails a **stable** note whose paths do not resolve; drafts may reference pending packs.
- `impact.md` at the Project root is an append-only ledger of six-field entries (`date, kind, targets, refs, outcome, reason`). `generate` appends publication entries automatically after each atomic publication to the canonical root; review decisions are appended procedurally. `validate` rejects malformed entries.
- Work items may declare `evidence_packs: [slugs]`; `check-completion` fails naming any declared pack that lacks a draft-or-stable note linking it via `evidence:`.
- Every Project has a vault-only `mathdocs/` registry. Stable Math Derivations carry the current script SHA-256, Python/SymPy versions, verification time, host, and source directory. Stable regular notes mark each display equation with a resolvable `MathDoc` result or exposition identifier.
- Task P proposal artifacts use `draft -> approved -> done` status and `pending -> accepted|rejected` decisions. `validate-proposal` checks a SHA-pinned curated input manifest, scope/independence policy, immutable fingerprints, execution-pack behavioral evidence, and project-relative candidate isolation. `check-completion` enforces the proposal gate before its Consumer Interface early return.

## Details
- `validate` checks packs and the ledger before pair validation; a vault with neither is unaffected (all keys optional).
- A pack with files missing from its manifest body — or listing files absent on disk — fails validation; packs are expected flat (one directory of payload files).
- Deprecated notes never satisfy evidence linkage; drafts do.
- `check-math --project PROJECT [--slug SLUG]` executes active derivations in lexical order with a bounded timeout, reports every selected file as PASS or FAIL plus a summary, and compares their versioned JSON protocol, environment, source hash, and named results against the paired notes. It warns that execution is trusted and not sandboxed.
- After reviewing changed symbolic output, `check-math --update --source-root REPO` stages all selected paired-note metadata and generated result regions, then publishes the complete `mathdocs/` tree or nothing. Update dependent regular notes and implementation from those published canonical results before rerunning `validate` and completion.
- Math-derived work items declare both `derivations` and a finite `math_implementation_files` list. `check-completion --source-root REPO` requires each source file to stay under that root and carry an adjacent `MathDoc: project/slug[#result]` identifier.
- Completion is record-local: `related_notes`, record `derivations` and those notes' declared derivations form the checked closure. Unrelated legacy defects do not block this check; declared missing/malformed/deprecated/stale dependencies do, including non-interface records. Non-mathematical records need no unrelated mathdocs registry. Identity, ancestry, acceptance, review, containment and receipt gates are unchanged.
- Consumer completion checks whole atomic Skill Pair integrity and the current source/routed reference for each declared Consumer note; unrelated source freshness belongs to full-vault validation. Named `check-math --slug` verifies/updates its selected pairs without parsing unrelated regular notes or altering unselected MathDoc bytes. `validate`, projection generation and unscoped `check-math` remain strict global audits.
- `check-installation` byte-compares both named-adapter packages and their Project identity against the canonical pair. Success proves on-disk installation only; reload the adapter and inspect its skill inventory before claiming active-session discovery.

### Existing library role recovery

`migrate-library` accepts the existing `kosmic.semantic-role-classification/v1`
map for in-place legacy Topic metadata recovery, separately from Project
Skill Pair migration. Each source must name its unchanged library-relative
Topic identity, explicit role and typed relationships. An optional
`source_project` pin must match existing provenance; without it the source
must belong to the governing Project. Typed Topics must already agree with
the assignment. Unclassified legacy dependencies and symlink sources or
generated outputs are rejected. Recovery preserves body bytes, validates
the complete staged library and publishes atomically. It cannot turn an
incomplete paragraph into a valid procedure; a separately approved and
reviewed content proposal must supply that repair.

## Flat-spec migration

`migrate-subprojects-plan --project PROJECT --output PLAN` saves an exclusive, hash-pinned JSON plan. It derives feature owners from declared ancestry and explicit assignments; it never approves work or moves source records. Ambiguous owners and unsupported live references must be resolved before application.

`migrate-subprojects-apply --project PROJECT --plan PLAN --approve-digest DIGEST --work-record REF` requires the exact reviewed plan digest and a currently approved or in-progress shared Quick Task in that Project. It recomputes the plan, rejects input drift and occupied or unsafe targets, validates a staged catalog, and publishes checked per-path changes with durable before images. It does not depend on the feature catalog being migrated for its bootstrap authority.

`migrate-subprojects-recover` takes the same arguments. It reconciles an interrupted transaction and restores incomplete application or verifies a complete cutover before writing its missing receipt. Unknown external edits are conflicts, not permission to overwrite them. Ordinary application failure restores original affected bytes and transaction-created directories.

Successful receipts map old paths and identities to the new owners. Reapplying the exact completed plan verifies its managed outputs and returns the existing receipt. Historical evidence, logs and lifecycle decisions remain unchanged; a migration receipt is not a work-completion receipt. Bound STATUS output uses final Project paths. An unbound Project stays unbound, and installed skills never change as part of this migration.

These commands run offline with Python's standard library and no model calls. Application requires a Git worktree with its managed `.tmp/` scratch root ignored. Migration execution and adapter installation retain separate approvals.

Frontmatter parsing accepts nested mappings and sequences, flow collections, and literal/folded block scalars without a third-party YAML dependency. Duplicate keys are rejected within each mapping; separate source entries may each contain `title`. Tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, complex keys, and tab indentation are unsupported and rejected.

The planner audits authoritative Project Markdown file by file, including root documents, specs, notes, and MathDocs. Local URL paths are matched separately from queries, fragments, and Markdown titles; external URLs and code examples stay unchanged. Valid references in staying documents retain their original bytes. A broken reference is repaired only when its filename or stem has one authoritative target; ambiguous matches block application. `link_corrections` records emitted repairs, and `link_problems` reports unresolved or protected references. Evidence, logs, and generated skills are pinned and audited, never rewritten. Symlinked source files or protected roots fail with `SCOPE_DENIED` rather than escaping the inventory.

A resolved YAML link whose scalar cannot be rewritten surgically is reported as `unsupported-link-rewrite` and blocks application; it is never silently dropped from the audit. Malformed authoritative frontmatter stops planning with a typed diagnostic naming the file and syntax error.

Proposal input manifests and curated snapshots under `specs/skill-proposals/inputs/` are protected evidence, not live specifications. Migration pins their hashes and audits references without rewriting their bytes. Placeholder frontmatter that cannot be parsed is reported as a protected `unparsable-document`, allowing authoritative planning to continue without changing the YAML contract or breaking input-manifest hashes.

Target validity and repair eligibility are separate: protected Markdown may be a valid link destination but never a filename/stem repair candidate. Moving an authoritative document rebases its links to existing protected targets without changing target bytes. Table WikiLinks preserve their escaped alias separator (`\|`) and fragment. Reference definitions must begin the physical Markdown line with at most three leading spaces; mid-line prose citations, including those following an inline code span, are not links to audit or rewrite.

Explicit links to existing regular Project-contained Markdown outside the
inventory (for example `research/`) are also valid, hash-pinned target-only
inputs. Their bytes are not scanned or rewritten and their filenames never
enter repair candidate indexes. Moving documents rebase Markdown and WikiLink
references; staying documents keep valid bytes. `linked_*` metadata gives
existing local targets the same precedence as inventoried targets. No-follow
file/parent reads reject symlink targets, and target drift invalidates the
plan. Internal `.git/`, `.tmp/` and `.kosmic/` paths are not target-only inputs.

For `linked_*` metadata, a valid document-relative destination takes precedence over a Project-root namesake. This preserves an existing owner's `SubprojectEntry.md` link `specs/prd.md` when a root-level PRD is also being migrated. If no document-relative target exists, legacy Project-relative metadata still resolves; other metadata keeps its established Project-relative precedence. Staged catalog validation must verify owner ancestry before publication, even when the plan reports no ownership ambiguity.
